II23A-01.note: Cadfield (heat only) vs Aldmoss (heat+dredge) isolates dredging. Tempting: C (Dellow vs Cadfield), which isolates heat; D runs the wrong direction for a dredged cove.

II23A-02.note: Logged-only Corlett lighter than worm-only Ambersley undercuts 'mainly worms'. A is the strongest lure but supports Brevard; C weakens the rival instead.

II23A-03.note: Common rural garden, ordinary seeds, city vs rural origin isolates evolution. Tempting: D (Esterholm heavy-seed confound) and A (different gardens).

II23A-04.note: Burn-only Daleford beating fence-only Carbery in the same pre-2010 year weakens fences. C is the cross-year wet-summer trap; B supports fences.

II23A-05.note: High-mite unsprayed Bramel storing less than low-mite sprayed Ardane favors mites over pesticide. D is the elevation trap; C reversed; B isolates pesticide.

II23A-06.note: Needs rats/area and chicks/nests for each island: only Benvoray (6.2/ha, 0.65) clears both. A (0.73 but 4.0 rats/ha) is the main lure; options print only chicks/nests so the rat ratio must be fetched.

II23A-07.note: Limit is 1.5 m above the bolt (1.1 + 0.4 offset); Dovell above vs Brockel below. D (Cendry 1.3) is the offset trap; A reversed; C both above.

II23A-08.note: Copperhill drops 8 points and ripens in 66 days. Birchtop is the lure (fast ripening but 13-point drop); option text omits the 25C value, so the table is required. Emberglow/Dawnlight fail on days by sight vs 71.

II23B-01.note: Leaky far-from-quarry Ingold beating sealed quarry-side Harrowfield on matched thick soil supports mains. B is the thin-soil confound lure; A reversed; C soil confound.

II23B-02.note: Meltwater-only Hamrin later than shade-only Isel supports Hovik. B isolates shade; C doubly confounded; D runs against meltwater.

II23B-03.note: Injection-only Gisler beating fracking-only Kvamby while both active. A confounds Hollis's fracking; D the fault-zone trap; C reversed in time.

II23B-04.note: Kvist (300 hikers) losing less than Gorrel (120), both horse-free and gentle, weakens hikers. B weakens horses instead; D slope confound; A horse confound.

II23B-05.note: No option cleanly weakens a steady-seepage-at-Gullhaven claim: A/D are Ljorn clay confounds, C is consistent with Hagelin, B only supports Laukvik across mismatched years. Possible defective item; key should be checked.

II23B-06.note: Ivesk 95 m, 18/8 = 2.25. Grinde (2.14 but 60 m) is the depth trap; Hallum 1.94 near-miss.

II23B-07.note: Iskilde fell 41->30 then rose 26.7%. Granberg rose >20% but never fell (1990 column needed); Ludal fell but rose only 15%.

II23B-08.note: Beyond-line set is Jassel/Kolbeck by closest approach; Jassel 3.4 >= 2x Gyllen 1.6. C (6.3 vs 3.5 = 1.8x) is the near-miss lure; B uses farthest-distance misreading (Ivra).

II23C-01.note: Stations-only Nettleford beating lanes-only Mossgate on flat ground weakens lanes. B terrain confound; C supports; D weakens the rival.

II23C-02.note: Mellick vs Pasterby on weekdays: both rail, no bus lanes, only Mellick charging. A/C rail confounds; B reversed.

II23C-03.note: Porch-only Nethercote vs neither Quellin (both pre-1994). B doubly confounded; A/D run against porches. Requires converting build dates into cul-de-sac status.

II23C-04.note: Neither-Ruskett adopting before extension-only Merrigal, both near market. C distance confound; D supports credit; A supports Okoro.

II23C-05.note: In 2017 Quorley is tax-only and Mistlow has nothing yet. D (Pendry before/after tax) is the lure but sits on a regional downtrend and a 2016 campaign; A isolates the campaign.

II23C-06.note: Line at +4 km: Moxley (6) outside beats Rindell (1) inside. B and D reversed; C both inside.

II23C-07.note: Mavisford 3.7 books/resident, 52 km. Ollerby clears the rate but is 18 km; Quintard/Pembray under 3 by quick division.

II23C-08.note: Quillow 81.8% completion and +$4.20. Prestley (83%, +$3.90) is the near-miss; option text omits enrollees and prior wage, so the table must be combined.

II23D-01.note: Sellwick's sales falling after its 1840 railway with nothing else changing. A supports; B/D market confounds.

II23D-02.note: Upland Stavely (40 yrs, off road) beats upland Tessaby (0, on road): school beats road. A (Vintrell vs Wrayburn) is the lure but carries a road confound.

II23D-03.note: Headland Sallowby (company) vs headland Vexley (ordinance). C reversed; B/D cross harbor-headland confounds.

II23D-04.note: 1851 Tenlow (mill rule, no board) beating Sudmere (board) undercuts boards. A is the slump-year confound lure; B supports; C weakens the rival.

II23D-05.note: Same-town clerk vs shopkeeper isolates installment access. B runs against; A/C mix in the conservatory.

II23D-06.note: Stennard 9,800->21,500 (2.19x). Options print only 1900 attendance; Ulvercote 1.87x near-miss; Tavisholm doubles but has 610 seats.

II23D-07.note: Tarnside 18.6 visitors/painting and 27.6% sold. Uxley (26% but 23 visitors/painting) and Yoxholt (17.9 but 23.8%) each fail one condition.

II23D-08.note: Vardleigh 8 outlets x 1,200 = 9,600 >= 9,400. Sedgeholm passes the ratio but has a grammar school; Wickerby/Ulsworth are near-misses.
